clue.text: Tough guy's brief: finding hot money

indicators.note: something brief is cut short, so the last letter of the tough-guy word is dropped

parts.note: a hard case is a tough, uncompromising person
H is the standard abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A hard man's lawyer turns up hot money, as in a crime drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' looks like a lawyer, as in British slang, but it tells you to shorten HARD CASE to HARDCAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard cash is money in notes and coins, as opposed to cheques or credit.

clue.text: Trouble as ship gets stuck in sound

indicators.note: the ship letters are lodged inside the word for sound

parts.note: sound and hale both mean healthy, as in hale and hearty
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A vessel runs aground in a stretch of water, causing problems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' suggests a stretch of sea, but it means healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Hassle is bother or trouble, as a noun for annoying difficulty.

clue.text: Theatre company takes on amateur show again

indicators.note: the theatre company takes on the next piece, with it added after

parts.note: rep is short for repertory, a resident theatre company
lay means non-professional or amateur

explanation.surface: A professional troupe hires amateurs for a revival.
explanation.definitionFit: To replay something is to broadcast or play it once more.

clue.text: Restaurants having terrible bar service as chief of baristas is absent

indicators.note: terrible service is messed up, so the remaining letters are jumbled
the letter is missing from the phrase bar service
the chief of baristas is its first letter

explanation.surface: Eating places with awful bar staff because the head barista is off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is absent' takes B (the chief of baristas) out of BAR SERVICE, leaving ARSERVICE; 'terrible' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Carveries are restaurants serving roast meat carved to order at a counter.

clue.text: Yarn about one man's unusual craft

indicators.note: the yarn word goes about, wrapping round, the other letters

parts.note: a yarn is a tale or story

indicators.note: unusual signals that the letters of one man's are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: A tale about one man's remarkable skill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yarn' tempts as knitting wool, tying in with 'craft', but it is a tale; 'unusual' signals the anagram and 'about' the wrapping.
explanation.definitionFit: Stonemasonry is the skilled trade of cutting and laying stone, a craft.

clue.text: Perfect advice to parliamentary leader

parts.note: a tip is a piece of useful advice

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, here of parliamentary

explanation.surface: Some excellent advice is passed to the head of a parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Tip-top is an informal adjective for excellent or perfect.

clue.text: Russian woman stuck in minivan apparently

indicators.note: the letters sit stuck inside the run of words minivan apparently

explanation.surface: A Russian lady seems to be trapped in a small van.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivana is a common Slavic female name, the feminine of Ivan.

clue.text: One visits Loire destination, extremely tacky and popular with sightseers

indicators.note: one goes into the city, entering it as a visitor would

parts.note: Tours is a city on the Loire in France
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: extremely takes the extreme letters of tacky, first and last

explanation.surface: A tourist goes to a Loire town that is gaudy and overrun with visitors.
explanation.definitionFit: Touristy describes a place crowded with tourists and catering to them, often tackily.

clue.text: It's on address label after 'cash on delivery', near bottom of package

parts.note: post is Latin for after, as in postwar

indicators.note: in a down entry the bottom of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Instructions on a parcel's label say payment is due on delivery, near the bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' and 'near' look like position words but 'after' gives POST and 'near' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A postcode is the alphanumeric code in a postal address, printed on the label.

clue.text: Better drink served to queen, having put away port

parts.note: to sup is to drink, and a sup is a mouthful

indicators.note: the queen's letters swallow the port, holding it inside

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the queen's royal cipher
Rio de Janeiro is a major Brazilian port

explanation.surface: A queen is served a finer drink after polishing off some port wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' suggests the fortified wine, fitting the drinking scene, but it is a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Superior and better are synonyms, both meaning higher in quality.

clue.text: Underground fighter runs from nobleman

indicators.note: the runs abbreviation is taken away from the title of the nobleman

parts.note: a marquis is a nobleman ranking above an earl
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A resistance fighter flees from an aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runs' reads as a verb of escape but is the letter R, removed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maquis were the French Resistance guerrillas of the Second World War, operating covertly.

clue.text: Goodness gracious! Soil-like deposit's reportedly found in desert

indicators.note: the sounded word is found inside the word for desert

parts.note: to forsake is to desert or abandon

indicators.note: reportedly means as spoken, so a word that sounds the same is used

parts.note: peat is a soil-like deposit of decayed vegetation, here with a possessive

explanation.surface: A deposit of earth turns up in a desert, to some surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desert' looks like sand, but it is the verb FORSAKE.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a mild exclamation of exasperation or surprise, like goodness gracious.

clue.text: Holiday the French have, being short of capital

parts.note: le is French for the

indicators.note: the word have loses its capital, meaning its first letter

explanation.surface: The French take a holiday while running low on funds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like money but means the initial letter H of HAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Leave is time off work, such as annual holiday or a soldier's furlough.

clue.text: Self-important type, say, Middle Easterner about to suffer setback

parts.note: e.g. means for example, as say does
an Omani is a person from Oman, on the Arabian Peninsula

indicators.note: a setback in a down-or-across entry means the word is read backwards here

parts.note: ca, from circa, means about

explanation.surface: A conceited Middle Eastern man, for instance, is about to suffer a reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: An egomaniac is obsessively absorbed in themselves, a self-important person to an extreme.

clue.text: Not pleased daughter has got the job?

parts.note: someone given a post is appointed to it

explanation.surface: A father wonders whether his daughter's new job is something to be glum about.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition and the split of the answer into D + IS APPOINTED tell different stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Disappointed means let down or displeased when hopes are unmet.

clue.text: By and large, Frenchman's upset, cuddled by popular girl

indicators.note: the girl comes by, next to, the popular piece

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: the reversed name is held inside the girl word, as if in an embrace

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl

indicators.note: in a down entry upset means turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: Rene is a typical French man's name

explanation.surface: A Frenchman is upset when a popular girl hugs him.
explanation.walkthrough: IN comes first in the answer although 'popular' comes last in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: In general and by and large are idioms both meaning usually or on the whole.

clue.text: Deal with shop ordering plant

indicators.note: ordering means putting the letters of deal and shop into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A garden shop places an order for a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Asphodel is a lily-like flowering plant, famed in Greek myth as covering the Elysian fields.

clue.text: Maybe rifleman curled lip, given alcoholic drink

indicators.note: in a down entry the lip curls back on itself, read from bottom up

parts.note: lager is a pale beer

explanation.surface: A soldier sneers when handed a beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rifleman' suggests a soldier, but here it is one who rifles through goods, a looter.
explanation.definitionFit: One who rifles, ransacking and stealing, is a pillager; 'Maybe' marks this as an example.

clue.text: Largely fashionable writer taking time in part of London

indicators.note: largely means most of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: swish means smart or fashionable
Sir Walter Scott was the Scottish novelist of Ivanhoe
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A smart author takes his time in a London district.
explanation.walkthrough: SWISS COTTAGE is an area of north-west London with an Underground station.
explanation.definitionFit: Swiss Cottage is a named district of the capital, near Hampstead.

clue.text: I'll follow men over North American state

indicators.note: the I word comes after, following, the men
in a down entry over means placed above the next piece

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers or men
the ego is the self, the I

explanation.surface: Someone vows to follow the men across the north of America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North American' looks like one phrase, but North is N.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregon is a US state on the Pacific coast.

clue.text: Thinner person who's not upstanding?

definitions.meaning: someone who leans rather than standing upright, a playful sense of not upstanding as not honest

explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of lean means slimmer, and one who leans tilts away from upright.

clue.text: Distinguishing features of booty Communist mentioned

indicators.note: mentioned means spoken out, so the pair of words is heard rather than read

parts.note: a haul is booty or loot, and Karl Marx is the founding Communist thinker

explanation.surface: Someone lists the telltale signs of a Communist's ill-gotten loot.
explanation.definitionFit: Hallmarks are characteristic marks, the typical traits that identify something.

clue.text: Opera overshadowed by Norma? No, never

indicators.note: the opera is concealed inside, overshadowed by, the words around it

explanation.surface: One opera is eclipsed by Bellini's Norma, says a fan emphatically.
explanation.definitionFit: Manon is Massenet's opera, also Puccini's Manon Lescaut, about Manon Lescaut.

clue.text: Regularly inquires re NHS worker

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter, here the even ones of the two words

explanation.surface: A health-service employee keeps making enquiries about something.
explanation.walkthrough: The NHS is Britain's National Health Service.
explanation.definitionFit: A nurse is a hospital worker, here one employed by the National Health Service.

clue.text: Create what's central to agenda? It's a bit of a fag

parts.note: to do something can mean to make or create it

indicators.note: the central letters of agenda, without its two ends, are taken

explanation.surface: Someone asks how to put together the core of a meeting's agenda, which proves a chore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fag' reads as a tedious task, but it is British slang for a cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog-end is the stub of a smoked cigarette, a small remnant of a smoke.

clue.text: Arrogant, rearranging plant

indicators.note: rearranging tells you the letters of arrogant are put in a new order

explanation.surface: An arrogant gardener reorganises his plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarragon is an aromatic herb grown for its leaves, used in French cookery.

clue.text: Tempting girl ultimately with posh item of jewellery

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of girl

parts.note: U is the label for upper-class usage, hence posh
a ring is worn on the finger as jewellery

explanation.surface: A girl is finally won over by a smart piece of jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: Luring means enticing or drawing someone in, which is tempting them.

clue.text: Comfy seat on front of cruise ship

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in letters

indicators.note: the front of cruise is its first letter

parts.note: a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: A comfortable deck chair sits at the bow of a cruise ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A recliner is an armchair whose back tilts for lounging, a comfortable chair.
